Subject: Capstone RFI: Request for control mapping and resilience appendix

Vivek —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement is consolidating our RFI responses and we need a few specific artifacts that must be included in the file we share with the audit/compliance team: 

- A control mapping that aligns Redwood controls to the FFIEC resilience domains (processes/people/technology) and the top-line control IDs we provided.
- A short resilience appendix (2–3 pages) that covers RTO/RPO targets for hosted vs. dedicated vs. private deployments, backup/retention policies, DR runbooks, and failover mechanics.
- Evidence references: SOC 2 Type II report, encryption attestations (in-transit & at-rest), and recent penetration-test summary (redacted OK).
- Point of contact for any follow-up technical deep-dive.

Can you share the mapping and appendix as editable artifacts (xlsx / pdf) by close of business Thursday (2026-03-12)? Procurement may loop in our third-party risk team for a quick 72-hour review.

Also note: we will need a short statement confirming data residency options (US-only or multi-region) and whether audit logs are available via API.

Appreciate it —
Alan

Alan —

Thanks, Vivek. Alan, I’ve completed the first-pass mapping and added commentary in the xlsx for each control. A few notes inline: 

- Controls mapping: each row maps to your control ID, a Redwood control description, control owner, evidence artifact (SOC2 section / Confluence page / Drive link), and whether the control is operationalized for Hosted / Dedicated / Private.
- RTO/RPO: Hosted: RTO = 60s token-stream failover for individual requests; for tenant-level recovery our documented restores target < 4 hours for stateful components (KV caches, persistent metadata). Dedicated: customer-configurable RTO down to 15 minutes with DR snapshotting. Private: depends on customer infra, we provide scripts and a runbook; typical RTO expectation is 4–24 hours. RPO: hosted default 0–5 minutes for ephemeral caches; persistent user data retained per the customer-configured retention policy (defaults to 30d).
- Backups & retention: backups are daily snapshots for persistent stores. Archive retention (cold) available up to 7 years for enterprise contracts.
- Encryption: in-transit TLS >=1.2 with HSTS; at-rest AES-256 with KMS-managed keys. For Private deployments customers may bring their own KMS/HSM.
- Audit logs: tenant-level audit logs are available via API with configurable retention; we include event types and sample curl examples in the appendix.

Attached artifacts in this email: SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2025.pdf (redacted), Encryption-KMS-Overview.pdf, and the working control mapping xlsx. I flagged 3 controls that are in progress (third-party monitoring integration) — we'll provide evidence once the vendor attestation is finalized next quarter.

I can join the Wednesday walkthrough to cover SOC2 and control evidence locations. If your team has a standardized control spreadsheet, send it over and I’ll drop our columns into your template.
